caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 11 of 2011
lawyer:
Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For Respondent ------ Not represented
parties:
Md. Yusuf Ali and others ------ Petitioners
VS
The State ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.5.2010 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 370 of 2000 dismissing the appeal thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 9.2.2000 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Jamalpur in Sessions Case No. 24 of 1997 arising out of G.R. No. 12(2)1997 corresponding to Bakshigonj Police Station Case No. 01 dated 07.01.1997 convicting the accused under sections 304 Part II / 114 of the Penal Code sentencing the convict appellant No. 1 Nur Islam to pay a fine of Tk. 20,000/- (Taka twenty thousand), in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 2 (two) years and the remaining four convict-appellants were each sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 (three) years and also to pay a fine of Tk. 3,000/-  (Taka three thousand), in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 5 (five) months more. It was further ordered that out of the fine amount of Tk. 27,000/- was to be paid to the heirs of the victim in accordance with Muslim Law of inheritance and remaining Tk. 5,000/- was to go to the State. 

 3. After investigation, the accused were put on trial to face charges brought against them under Sections 304/114/34 of the Penal Code. The accused pleaded not guilty to the charge. Twelve witnesses were examined by the prosecution and the accused were examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure when they again pleaded not guilty, but did not lead any evidence. After considering all the evidence and materials on record, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jamalpur convicted and sentenced the convict appellants as mentioned above. 

 5. The learned Counsel Mr. Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that there was no eye witness to the occurrence and since the victim died many days after the occurrence, conviction under sections 304/114 of the Penal Code was illegal and the conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He further submits that from the evidence on record it is clear that both the informant (P.W.1) and her son (P.W.2) went to the place of occurrence after hearing the cries of the victim and, therefore, they could not have seen the occurrence. He also submits that the learned Judges of the Courts below misread the evidence when considering P.Ws. 1 and 2 to be eye witnesses. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the only physical blow by dao is attributed to accused Yusuf and no other injury is found on the victim and, therefore, the conviction and sentence of the accused convicts other than Md. Yusuf Ali is dot sustainable in law and, therefore, their appeal ought to have been allowed. 

 6. We have heard Mr. Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Counsel for the petitioners and perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division as well as that of the trial Court along with the evidence and materials on record. 

 7. It is an admitted fact that the victim Mostafa died of tetanus resulting from an injury to the middle finger of his left hand. The trial Court found P.Ws. 1 and 2 to be eye witnesses of the occurrence. We do not find any reason to disagree with that finding of fact that an altercation took place between the victim and the accused Nur Islam, which is supported by independent witnesses, who were declared hostile by the prosecution. Immediately after the altercation, the occurrence took place where the victim received a cut injury to the middle finger of his left hand, which developed infection and led to the victim's death due to tetanus. On the assessment of the evidence, the trial Court also found that the accused did not injure the victim with intention to kill him and therefore, took a lenient view when awarding sentence upon them. 

 8. The High Court Division observed that the evidence of the witnesses show that the victim Mostafa repulsed the dao blow given to him at the order of accused Nurul Islam and had the victim not repulsed such blow, it would have been a fatal blow to cause his immediate death. However, the High Court Division also found that on the spur of the moment Mostafa sustained injury on his finger which subsequently caused tetanus and led to his death. 

 9. Considering the way in which the trial Court had properly appreciated the evidence on record, the High Court Division found no reason to interfere with the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court. 

 10. Having considered all the materials before us, we also find that the trial Court properly appreciated the evidence on record and awarded sentence having taken a lenient view.
